Guaranteed MIN/MAX limits exist only for GAIN(dVdT) 23.75/25.5 V/V (L453), I(OL)@12k 0.95/1.05 A (L461), I(CB)@120k MODE-open 0.045/0.11 A (L478), I(CB)@5.36k 2.0/2.4 A (L480), V(REVTH) -15/-5 mV (L530). The delays are TYPICAL-ONLY with NO published maximum: tCB(dly) 4 ms (L642), tFASTRIP(dly) 250 ns (L615), tCBretry(dly) 540 ms (L644), tdVdT 10 ms at 47 nF and 23.9 V/1.6 ms with dVdT open (L635-L636, L1365); therefore no max delay is claimed anywhere in this delivery. blocking_issues: No native TPS26601 dynamic model is executable: both vendor libraries (SLVMBY3 PSpice, SLVMBY4 TINA) remain encrypted and were not decryptable; substitution is forbidden, so startup behaviour is unproven.
The vendor TPS26601 model does not model temperature-dependent behaviour, so no hot-state or SOA conclusion can come from it even in principle.
No bypass hardware and no bypass model exist for the independent precharge+bypass route; the |Vin-Vout|<=1 V enable condition is a proposal, not a qualified design.
All eFuse protection delays (tCB(dly), tFASTRIP(dly), tCBretry(dly), tdVdT) are TYPICAL-ONLY in TPS2660.txt with no published maximum, so no worst-case delay can be claimed from the datasheet.
Arithmetic results (slew rate, 0-26.4 V rise, Pmax vs 6 W, 0.5 ohm, startup 0.5*C*U^2) require the principal to execute startup_arith.py; this worker did not run it and claims no computed value.
